title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

errors: No real error. As stated, 'exactly two classes' needs connectedness and regularity; both are assumed. The real content is that the generated relation does not collapse the two classes, i.e. no orientation-reversing loop exists. That is a genuine argument and is deferred to the following pages. 'De façon unique' should be read as unique once the 2-sets are identified; there is no ambiguity, since everything is canonical up to the global swap encoded in ω itself.

ideas.what: Combinatorial models (L, S, ∂) of 1-dimensional topological forms, built from points, segments and endpoint maps; decomposition into connected components and reduction to connected regular models
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial/axiomatic models of 1-dimensional spaces (cf. tame topology, o-minimal 1-dimensional cell structures, graphs/1-complexes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (classification of 1-manifolds; cell complexes); tame topology programme proposed by Grothendieck in Esquisse; o-minimality by van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) calls for a 'topologie modérée' but does not contain this axiomatics

ideas.what: Orientation 2-set ω of a connected regular 1-dimensional model, defined as the colimit of compatible bijections between endpoint pairs ∂I and local side-pairs B_x; there are exactly two equivalence classes
ideas.modern_name: Orientation torsor / orientation double cover (trivial for connected 1-manifolds); orientability of 1-manifolds
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical algebraic topology (orientation covers; classification of 1-manifolds)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but standard combinatorial set-up: reduction to connected components, and a statement that a connected 1-dimensional model has a canonical two-element orientation set. Mathematically routine. Its only interest is as a piece of Grothendieck's unpublished attempt at a combinatorial 'geometry of forms' (tame topology), which is already known historically.
transcription_corrections: First line likely reads '; on se ramène aussitôt à ses comp. connexes' rather than '; ce [?] revient [?] à [?] ses comp.'
'Donc l'étude des modèles X réguliers revient à celle des modèles réguliers connexes' (the struck word is 'est'; 'revient à' is followed by 'celle des')
The theorem line reads 'Th. On peut trouver, (de façon unique), un syst. transitif d'iso entre les ∂I (I∈S)'; the dangling 'de façon unique)' above is the insertion intended for this parenthesis.
'un quotient ω_S' / 'un quotient ω_L' are probably preceded by 'd'où' (hence) rather than 'donc'.
'(soit ω le quotient)' — ω is underlined in the manuscript (bold-like notation).
